category: managed authoritative DNS and traffic steering

free_tier.stated: a 30-day free trial with 50M DNS queries/month, 500 DNS records, 20 health check monitors, 10 traffic steering chains, 50 HTTPS redirects, Cloud Sync and zone versioning; no credit card required at sign-up
free_tier.notes: This is a time-boxed trial, not a recurring free allowance. The trial is the only no-charge entry; no permanent free tier was found on the pricing page.

per_object_cap.stated: 500 DNS records in the trial; a DNS record may hold multiple answers, and the maximum TTL on a record is 86400 seconds (24 hours), with values above that automatically adjusted to 86400
per_object_cap.notes: The 86400-second TTL ceiling is from the DNS-record documentation and applies to records in all zones, not to the trial alone.

retention.stated: unverified: no data-deletion or retention period after the 30-day trial ends is stated on the pages read
retention.notes: Zone records survive only while the account and its subscription or trial remain active; the exact post-trial deletion window is unverified.

egress.terms: DNS queries are counted against a monthly allowance (50M DNS queries/month on the trial); no per-GB traffic price is published, since DNS is priced by query count rather than by bytes out

interface_detail: a REST API at https://api.nsone.net/v1 (legacy) and https://api.nsone.net/{category}/v1 (newer) returning JSON over HTTPS, authenticated with an API key secret in the X-NSONE-Key header; the first key must be created in the NS1 Connect portal; a web portal manages zones and records
tooling: REST API through curl or any HTTP client with an X-NSONE-Key API key; the NS1 Terraform provider (ns1-terraform/ns1) is the documented infrastructure-as-code path; Ansible integration is listed on the product page
chaining: managed authoritative DNS with real-time traffic steering, health-check monitors and HTTPS redirects; Cloud Sync synchronises zones with Amazon Route 53 as a paid add-on, and a Terraform toolkit keeps zones in step with other providers

limits.value: 500 DNS records (trial); TTL capped at 86400 seconds (24 hours)
20 health check monitors and 10 traffic steering chains (trial)

binding_note: the 50M DNS queries/month trial allowance is the first quantity an active zone consumes; the 500-record and 20-monitor caps are far above a single zone's needs

identity_cost.detail: the trial sign-up page asks for a business email address, first name, last name, country and password to create an IBMid; Company is a required field in the form metadata; no credit card is required ('Create your account. No credit card required.'); a phone number and an ID document are not requested on the form read (https://www.ibm.com/account/reg/signup?formid=urx-54055)

reliability_note: the API requires HTTPS and rejects plain HTTP or unauthenticated requests; the Terraform provider documentation warns that 429 rate-limit responses occur and recommends rate_limit_parallelism 60; no outage history was read
confidence_note: first-party pricing, signup, product, API, Terraform and DNS-record pages were read and quoted; every value is at documented rung, with no live trial measurement of post-trial behaviour
